title: DP Geography or Economics vs MYP I&S Difficulty
summary: Compare DP Geography and Economics with MYP Individuals and Societies, including workload, assessment, subject choice, and practical preparation.
body_markdown:
Moving from MYP Individuals and Societies to DP Geography or Economics is a significant but manageable step up. The main change is not simply learning more content. You must use subject-specific terminology, apply formal methods, recall detailed evidence, and produce analytical answers under tighter examination conditions.


Neither DP subject is automatically harder. **Geography** usually suits students who enjoy spatial patterns, environmental and social issues, data interpretation, and case studies. **Economics** often suits students who prefer structured theories, diagrams, logical reasoning, and policy evaluation.


### How much harder is the move from MYP to DP?


There is no official difficulty multiplier, but most students find DP Geography or Economics substantially more demanding than MYP Individuals and Societies. MYP develops broad inquiry, communication, research, and critical-thinking skills. DP expects you to apply those skills within a defined academic discipline and demonstrate them in externally assessed examinations.


The[official MYP Individuals and Societies subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief_individuals-societies_2015.pdf) organizes assessment around four equally weighted criteria: **Knowing and understanding, Investigating, Communicating, and Thinking critically** . These provide a strong foundation, but DP assessment is more closely tied to prescribed content, subject-specific techniques, command terms, and examination mark schemes.


Area MYP Individuals and Societies DP Geography or Economics


Scope Often interdisciplinary and shaped by the school A defined specialist subject


Knowledge Broad concepts and selected contexts More prescribed content and terminology


Evidence Sources, examples, and classroom research Case studies, data, models, or diagrams


Writing Varied criterion-based tasks Timed responses matched to commands and marks


Assessment Mainly school-based, with optional eAssessment External examinations and compulsory internal assessment


Independence Guided inquiry and projects Sustained revision and coursework management


The transition feels largest during the first term because students learn content and a new assessment language simultaneously. Understanding commands such as **explain** , **analyse** , **evaluate** , and **discuss** makes expectations more predictable.


### What changes in DP Geography?


[DP Geography](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/geography/) combines human, physical, and environmental geography. Students study interactions among people, places, processes, and environments at different scales. It may therefore feel familiar to MYP students who have studied population, migration, development, hazards, climate, resources, or sustainability.


The difficulty comes from depth. Instead of identifying causes of urban growth, for example, you may need to interpret unfamiliar data, explain a process, integrate a detailed case study, compare scales, and evaluate management strategies.


You must develop four main areas:


- **Case-study knowledge:** Recall specific places, processes, policies, and outcomes accurately.
- **Geographical analysis:** Explain patterns rather than merely describing maps or graphs.
- **Extended writing:** Build focused arguments using evidence, evaluation, and reasoned conclusions.
- **Fieldwork:** Complete an internal assessment involving data collection, analysis, and evaluation.


The IB’s[Geography subject brief and assessment overview](https://ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/geography-sl-hl-2017-en.pdf) describes structured, stimulus-based, and extended-response questions. HL adds breadth and a stronger synoptic dimension. Check the guide for your examination cohort because curricula and assessments can change.


### What changes in DP Economics?


[DP Economics](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/economics/) studies choices made under scarcity through microeconomics, macroeconomics, and the global economy. Prior Economics study helps but is not normally necessary because the course introduces its concepts systematically.


Economics becomes difficult when several skills must appear in one response. A question about an indirect tax may require a definition, correctly labelled diagram, explanation of price and quantity changes, real-world application, and evaluation of whether the policy will work.


The subject demands:


- **Precise terminology** with meanings narrower than everyday usage.
- **Model-based reasoning** connecting diagrams directly to written analysis.
- **Real-world application** involving recognizable markets, economies, and policies.
- **Evaluation** of assumptions, stakeholders, time periods, consequences, and alternatives.
- **Quantitative work** , with additional depth at HL.


Under the current[Economics SL subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/sl-economics-en.pdf) , SL students complete two external papers and a portfolio of three commentaries. The IA contributes **30%** of the SL grade. The[Economics HL subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/hl-economics-en.pdf) adds a policy paper, while the commentary portfolio contributes **20%** of the HL grade.


### Is Geography or Economics the easier transition?


The answer depends on how you think, not simply on your MYP grade.


Geography may suit you if you enjoy Economics may suit you if you enjoy


Maps, graphs, and spatial patterns Logical models and causal chains


Environmental and social issues Markets, governments, and policy choices


Detailed case studies Drawing and explaining diagrams


Scientific and social perspectives Applying theory to current events


Fieldwork and primary data Structured argument and quantitative interpretation


Geography may initially feel more familiar because many MYP courses contain geographical units. Its challenge is the volume of examples and the precision required when explaining processes. Economics can feel less familiar, but recurring models make it highly structured once the foundations are secure.


Do not choose Geography because it is described as common sense or reject Economics because it contains calculations. Read your school’s course outline, inspect representative questions, and consider which weekly tasks suit your strengths.


### Which MYP skills transfer directly?


Several MYP skills remain valuable. **Criterion A** supports accurate knowledge, **Criterion B** prepares you for research and coursework, **Criterion C** develops organized communication, and **Criterion D** supports analysis and evaluation.


In DP, these skills become discipline-specific. Saying that a policy has advantages and disadvantages is insufficient. You must identify affected groups, explain the mechanism, weigh evidence, and reach a judgement addressing the exact question.


The[RevisionDojo MYP Individuals and Societies resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-individuals-and-societies) can reinforce foundations such as scarcity, development, trade, population, urban systems, and environmental change.


### How to prepare before DP begins


### Learn command terms


Write short answers using **describe** , **explain** , **analyse** , and **evaluate** , checking that the level of thinking changes with each command. This prevents descriptive responses to analytical questions.


### Strengthen core knowledge


For Geography, revise population change, climate processes, resources, development, sustainability, and map interpretation. For Economics, begin with scarcity, opportunity cost, supply, demand, equilibrium, inflation, unemployment, growth, and trade.


### Build an evidence bank


Geography students should record each case study’s location, process, evidence, stakeholder perspectives, and limitations. Economics students can collect current examples of taxes, subsidies, interest-rate decisions, trade restrictions, and development policies. Several flexible, well-understood examples are better than a long list you cannot apply.


### Introduce timed practice gradually


Begin with one paragraph in ten minutes. Review its knowledge, application, analysis, and judgement, then extend the task once your structure becomes reliable.


The[IB Geography Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-geography/questionbank) and[IB Economics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-economics/questionbank) support the move from review to exam-style application. The guide to[writing IB Economics essays](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/step-by-step-approach-to-writing-ib-economics-essays) also explains question interpretation and evaluation.


### Common transition mistakes


- **Relying on general knowledge:** DP rewards accurate disciplinary knowledge.
- **Memorizing without applying:** Evidence must support the specific question.
- **Ignoring diagrams or data:** These are central forms of evidence.
- **Writing everything you know:** Relevance matters more than length.
- **Delaying coursework:** Fieldwork and commentaries require sustained planning.
- **Choosing by reputation:** An allegedly easy subject may not suit your methods.


### Conclusion


DP Geography and Economics are both harder than MYP Individuals and Societies because they require greater depth, independent recall, subject-specific techniques, and timed performance. Geography emphasizes spatial analysis, case studies, data, and fieldwork, while Economics emphasizes models, diagrams, application, and policy evaluation.


Your MYP experience still provides a valuable foundation in inquiry, communication, and critical thinking. Strengthen terminology, practise command terms, build an evidence bank, and begin short timed responses before DP. RevisionDojo’s[Geography resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-geography) and[Economics resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-economics) can support this progression through Study Notes, Flashcards, Questionbank practice, and Jojo AI feedback.
